Write an AOEF file

Source: R/aoef.R
writeAOEF.Rd

Writes a list of Annotation objects to a file in the Acoustic Objects Exchange Format (AOEF), as an annotation set or as an annotation project, which the soundevent Python package and the Whombat annotation tool (Balvanera et al. 2023) read.

Usage

writeAOEF(
  annotations,
  file,
  audio.dir = NULL,
  collection = "annotation_set",
  name = NULL,
  description = NULL
)

Arguments

annotations

A list of Annotation objects, or a single one.

file

Path to the AOEF file to write.

audio.dir

The directory the paths of the recordings are to be written relative to, which every annotated file must be in. Where it is NULL the paths are written as the annotations have them.

collection

One of "annotation_set" or "annotation_project". Whombat imports only annotation projects, which are annotation sets with a task for each clip, and whose tags, the ones offered to those annotating it, are every tag written.

name, description

A name and a description of the collection. An annotation project is named after the file where no name is given.

Value

Invisibly, the path of the file written.

Details

Each annotation is written as a sound event, tagged with its type as the key and its value as the value. An annotation with a value and no type is tagged with the key "label", and one with neither is written without a tag. Its shape is a stretch of time where it has no frequency limits, a single moment where it also starts where it ends, and otherwise a box of time and frequency, or a single point where the box has no size. An end of Inf is the end of the recording, and a high frequency of Inf above a low one is half the sample rate.

Annotations read by readAOEF() are written back as they were read: those of one sound event with several tags as one sound event again, a line or polygon as that shape where its range has not been changed, the tags of a clip on that clip, and each sound event in the clip it was in, under the identifiers it had. A sound event moved off its clip altogether is put in a clip spanning its recording, and one of several tags given a range of its own becomes a sound event of its own. Whombat imports the annotations of a project only for recordings it already holds under the same identifiers, which those annotations keep. The identifiedBy of an annotation is written as who made it (created_by) and its dateIdentified as when (created_on), where that is a single date and time of day: AOEF holds no date without a time, and one is not made up, nor a range. notes and features in the metadata of an annotation are written; nothing else of it is, so predictions are written as annotations without their scores.

soundevent reads only annotations in a clip, so every other annotation is put in a clip spanning the whole of its recording. AOEF also needs the duration, channels and sample rate of each recording, which are read from the file of the annotation, or taken from what readAOEF() kept of it. Reading a file other than a wave file needs the av package.

Characters outside ASCII are written as escapes, so that the file reads the same whatever encoding a reader takes it to be in.

References

Balvanera SM, Mac Aodha O, Weldy MJ, Pringle H, Browning E, Jones KE (2023). “Whombat: An open-source annotation tool for machine learning development in bioacoustics.” doi:10.48550/arXiv.2308.12688 . 2308.12688, https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12688.
